newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy Senate extends budget amendment deadline.
newsitem.headline: Italy Senate extends budget amendment deadline.

text.p: The leaders of Italy's political parties in the Senate (upper house) said they had extended until 0900 GMT on Thursday a deadline for presentation of amendments to the government's 1997 budget.

The original deadline for amendments to be submitted to the budget commission was 1900 GMT on Wednesday, when the centre-left government had been due to outline changes of its own to its controversial budgetary "Euro-tax."
The one-off levy, to be paid next year, is designed to raise 12.5 trillion lire ($8.3 billion) to help get Italy in shape to be a founder member of a single European currency in 1999.
Prodi's overall budget is designed to slash 62.5 trillion lire off next year's projected deficit.
